entries: Work order and lumber inspection｜Read specifications, cutting dimensions and quantity, measure raw material and identify defects such as cracks.｜Output a usable lumber list, cutting marks and items to confirm.

Finished goods and shift handoff｜Record conforming pieces, pieces awaiting measurement, waste and unfinished orders separately and hand them to the next responsible person.｜Output traceable quantities, versions and open items.

values: Fictional materials: lumber and cutting requirements

M1｜The paper order requires six finished boards, each 1,200 mm long, 90 mm wide and 18 mm thick; the length tolerance is ±2 mm. Use fictional materials only for planning; do not enter the workshop or operate equipment.

M2｜Stock has four boards, all 3,000 mm long with conforming width and thickness, numbered A, B, C and D. A, B and C look intact; D has a through crack 900–1,100 mm from one end and must not be used as conforming material for this exercise.

M3｜For ease of paper calculation, assume each finished piece requires one complete cut and each cut loses 3 mm of kerf; this problem ignores end trimming or extra clamping allowance. If the real process has different loss or clamping conditions, this calculation cannot be used directly for production scheduling.
Fictional materials: inspection and anomalies

M4｜The paper work order requires recording each finished piece's number, measured length and defect observations; pieces outside the 1,198–1,202 mm range or showing cracks should be isolated for review and not treated as conforming delivery.

M5｜The equipment check card before the planned start shows the guard functioning normally. The fictional event card at 09:20 shows the guard fastener is loose; the on-site operator immediately stops work and hands the equipment to authorized maintenance and safety staff for inspection. The paper exercise must not ask the reader to repair or test-cut it themselves.

M6｜The handoff must state conforming stock, planned piece count, loss assumptions, measured results, unfinished pieces, the guard anomaly, the stopped state and the recipient; this problem provides no repair completion or restart permission.
Task: plan first, then judge

T1｜First calculate how many 1,200 mm finished pieces each conforming 3,000 mm board can yield at most under the M3 assumptions, and how many conforming raw boards six finished pieces need at minimum; use D's crack as the exclusion reason. Write the planned output and remaining length for each raw board.

T2｜Use M4 to make a six-row inspection record template, writing the conforming length range and the defect judgment; rows without measured data stay as pending measurement and must not be filled in as conforming on your own.

T3｜After receiving M5, write a stop and handoff card: known faults, cuts and inspections not yet completed, who has authority to inspect the equipment, and what evidence is missing before restarting; the conclusion of this problem should allow that production scheduling cannot continue.
Reference approach and boundaries

Under the simplified conditions of M3, two finished pieces require 2×1,200+2×3=2,406 mm, leaving 594 mm; a third piece requires a total length of 3×1,200+3×3=3,609 mm, which exceeds 3,000 mm. Therefore plan two pieces each for A, B and C, six in total; D is not counted in conforming stock because of the crack.

The conforming length range for M4 is 1,198–1,202 mm (inclusive); without measured readings it can only be marked as pending measurement. After the guard anomaly in M5, work stops and is handed to authorized staff; without a repair record and restart approval, the paper capacity is not written as actual delivery and the reader is not asked to operate the saw.

subject.summary: Sawing machine setters, operators and tenders, wood, set up, operate or tend wood sawing equipment to work order specifications, check lumber defects, adjust blades and feed, and measure finished dimensions. When material jams, guards are abnormal or blades are worn, stop the machine and follow the on-site authorization procedure; this job is not the same as carpentry furniture making or independent CNC programming.
